autumn-ivy

A few sprigs of ivy turn red and gold in autumn, painted in a few quick strokes with a fresh, flowing style. Ogata Kenzan was a famous potter and painter in Kyoto and the younger brother of the painter Ogata Kōrin. He painted and decorated pottery with seasonal plants. It's a quiet picture that celebrates the beauty of the passing season.
irises-at-yatsuhashi-eight-bridges

Purple irises with green leaves grow in a zigzag across a folding screen of glittering gold, with a bridge made of eight planks. Ogata Kōrin painted this around 1710 based on a famous story from The Tales of Ise, a classic Japanese tale. The flat shapes and rich colors are like a beautiful pattern. It's one of the most famous Japanese paintings and a national treasure in Japan.
hotei

A round, cheerful monk with a big belly and a bag, Hotei, is painted with a few quick, playful strokes. Hotei is a happy god of good luck in Japanese and Chinese tradition. Ogata Kōrin drew him with simple lines and a lot of humor. It's a friendly picture that makes people smile.
rough-waves

Wild waves curl and crash in swirling gold and blue patterns on a folding screen, with white foam like tiny claws. Ogata Kōrin painted this in the early 1700s, and the waves look both realistic and like a design. Years later, Hokusai would paint his famous wave. It's one of the great sea pictures of Japan.
red-and-white-plum-blossoms

Two plum trees, one with red blossoms and one with white, stand on either side of a curving stream of dark swirling water, on a gold background. Ogata Kōrin made this pair of folding screens around 1715, and it is a national treasure of Japan. The stream in the middle looks like a decoration but is carefully designed. It's one of the most famous works of Japanese art.
actor-arashi-rikan-ii-as-osome

A kabuki actor plays the role of a young woman in a colorful woodblock print. Ryūsai Shigeharu was a printmaker in Osaka who made pictures of famous kabuki actors, which fans collected. The actor's pose and costume show the drama of the theater. It's a snapshot of the stage in old Japan.
flowering-plants-of-summer-and-autumn

Wildflowers and grasses sway in the wind on a pair of silver screens, with morning glories and bush clover. Sakai Hōitsu, a painter from Edo (Tokyo), wanted to continue the style of Ogata Kōrin. He painted the plants in soft colors. It's a lovely picture of the changing seasons.
flames

A woman in a robe stands in a swirl of orange-red flames, her hair and clothing streaming behind her. Uemura Shōen, one of Japan's greatest women painters, painted this in 1918, based on a legend of jealousy from a Noh play. The flames seem to come from her own feelings. It's a powerful picture by a master artist.
morning-glories

Blue and white morning glories climb up and fill the screen with green vines, in a bright, modern-looking design. Suzuki Kiitsu, a Japanese painter from Edo, was a student of Sakai Hōitsu. The flowers seem to float in the air. It's a graceful picture of a summer flower.
mountain-streams-in-summer-and-autumn

Rushing streams run through mountains, with trees in the bright greens of summer and the reds of autumn. Suzuki Kiitsu painted the seasons on a pair of screens. The curving water adds a flowing rhythm. It's a lovely way to see time pass in one picture.
tabby-cat

A fluffy tabby cat looks out at us with bright green eyes, sitting calmly with its fur painted in very fine lines. Takeuchi Seihō was a master painter from Kyoto who loved animals. The picture became a cultural treasure of Japan. It is one of the most famous cat paintings in the world.
night-rain-at-karasaki-from-the-series-eight-views-of-o

A giant, ancient pine tree stands at the edge of Lake Biwa on a rainy night, with the rain pouring down in dark lines. Utagawa Hiroshige made this woodblock print in the 1830s as part of a series of Eight Views of Ōmi. The tree and the soft ink gradations create a moody, magical feel. It's one of his most famous landscapes.
sudden-shower-over-shin-ohashi-bridge-and-atake

People hurry across a wooden bridge in a sudden rainstorm, with sheets of rain falling in black lines, and rafts on the river below. Utagawa Hiroshige made this woodblock print in 1857, and Vincent van Gogh was so struck by it that he copied it in oil. The lines of rain and the dark clouds are dramatic. It's one of the most famous prints in Japan.
plum-park-in-kameido

A huge plum tree branch stretches across the picture in the foreground, with a garden full of blossoms in the distance. Utagawa Hiroshige made this woodblock print in 1857 as part of One Hundred Famous Views of Edo. Vincent van Gogh copied it in oil paint in 1887 and showed how much he admired Japanese art. It's a bold and beautiful print.
one-hundred-horses-draft

A first sketch for the famous painting of one hundred horses, with horses resting, swimming and playing in a landscape. Giuseppe Castiglione was an Italian missionary and painter who became the court painter of the Chinese emperors. He combined Western realism with Chinese painting. It's a rare look at how he planned a masterpiece.
eight-horses

Eight horses of different colors stand and pose in a calm landscape. Giuseppe Castiglione, known in China as Lang Shining, painted the emperor's favorite horses. His lifelike style, with shadows and shapes, was new for Chinese painting. It's a handsome picture of the emperor's stable.
the-qianlong-emperor-in-ceremonial-armor-on-horseback

The Qianlong Emperor sits on a horse in shining armor, in a formal portrait. Giuseppe Castiglione painted the emperor in 1739, mixing Western realism with Chinese traditions. Qianlong ruled China for 60 years in the 1700s. It's a proud portrait of one of China's greatest emperors.
ayusi-sweeping-bandits-with-a-lance

A brave warrior, Ayusi, charges with a lance in a battle scene. Giuseppe Castiglione painted this to honor a hero of Emperor Qianlong's military campaigns in the 1750s. The dashing horse and rider are very lively. It's a great action picture from imperial China.
portrait-of-the-kangxi-emperor-in-informal-dress-holdin

The Kangxi Emperor sits in a relaxed pose, holding a brush, in a plain robe. The emperor ruled China for 61 years, longer than anyone else, and he painted and wrote poetry as well. This portrait shows him as a scholar, not only a ruler. It's a thoughtful picture of an emperor.
prosperous-suzhou

A huge scroll full of thousands of people, shops, boats and bridges shows a busy day in the city of Suzhou in the 1700s. Xu Yang, a court painter, spent years on it, painting every shop and sign in detail. You can spend hours finding little scenes of daily life. It's one of the most famous city scenes in Chinese art.
the-qianlong-emperor-s-southern-inspection-tour-scroll-

A long scroll painting shows the Qianlong Emperor's procession as it travels along a canal, with boats and crowds. Xu Yang was one of the court painters who recorded the tour in a series of giant scrolls. Each scroll is full of details of the landscape and the people. It's a grand record of an imperial journey.
the-qianlong-emperor-s-southern-inspection-tour-scroll--xu-yang

Another scroll from the series shows the emperor's travels through towns and countryside, with tiny people and boats on the river. Xu Yang painted twelve scrolls about the Qianlong Emperor's tour of southern China. They are among the largest and most detailed pictures from the Qing court. It's a fascinating look at life in 18th-century China.
haremde-goethe

The German poet Goethe, in a dressing gown, reads a book in a room full of women in an imagined Ottoman harem. Abdülmecid II painted this in 1918, and he was the last caliph of the Ottoman family and also a talented painter. It shows how Ottoman artists were interested in European culture. It's a very unusual meeting of East and West.
the-doshan-tappeh-street

A street in Tehran, with a few walls and trees in the afternoon sun. Kamal-ol-Molk was a leading Iranian painter who studied European techniques and painted scenes of everyday life in Persia. The detailed realism is typical of his style. It's a window into 19th-century Iran.
bagh-shah-square

A large public square in Tehran with people going about their day. Kamal-ol-Molk, the court painter of Iran, painted what he saw with a European realism that was new in Persia. It's an important record of what the city looked like. It's a historical snapshot.
mirror-hall

A grand palace hall with walls of mirrors and a glittering ceiling, where a man in robes sits in the middle. Kamal-ol-Molk painted this masterpiece of the Golestan Palace in Tehran in 1896. The mirrors and glass reflect light in a dazzling way. It's his most famous painting.
the-zoka-ol-molk-i

A thoughtful man in traditional Iranian dress looks out in a realistic portrait. Kamal-ol-Molk painted a number of portraits of Iranians in the early 1900s. The detail in the face and clothing is careful. It's a good example of Iranian realism.
coffee-table

A simple low table is set with coffee cups, a tray and some small items, with careful detail. Osman Hamdi Bey was a leading Ottoman painter and also the founder of Turkey's first archaeological museum. He painted objects with the same care he gave to his scientific work. It's a quiet still life.
girl-reciting-qur-an

A young girl in a long dress sits and reads from the Qur'an, in a quiet and peaceful scene. Osman Hamdi Bey painted this in the 1880s. The soft light and her calm face are gentle. It's a tender picture of faith and learning in Istanbul.
a-lady-of-constantinople

An elegant woman in a long dress sits calmly, in the rich colors of an Ottoman room. Osman Hamdi Bey studied painting in Paris, and he brought European skills back to Istanbul. The detail of the fabric and tiles is lovely. It's a graceful portrait.
mihrab

A woman sits in front of a beautifully tiled prayer niche, in a mosque or a shrine, with a calm, thoughtful look. Osman Hamdi Bey painted the tiles in great detail, because he knew Ottoman art very well. The blue tiles are brilliant. It's a lovely picture of Ottoman art and architecture.
old-man-in-front-of-children-s-graves

An old man stands in a graveyard, with children's graves nearby, in a sad and quiet scene. Osman Hamdi Bey painted this in 1903, and it's a strong picture of grief. The simple garden and tombstones are painted with great care. It's one of his best-known pictures.
family-of-general-don-felipe-codallos

A Mexican general, his wife and children pose together in their finest clothes in a formal portrait. Agustín Arrieta was a painter from Puebla, Mexico, who painted portraits and scenes of everyday life. The details of the clothes and furniture are careful. It's a glimpse of Mexican society in 1838.
san-pascual-bailon

A saint stands in a kitchen holding a pot, in a simple and colorful scene. San Pascual Bailón is the patron saint of cooks in Mexico, and he is shown among pots and kitchenware. Agustín Arrieta was famous for kitchens and still lifes. It's a charming picture of Mexican faith and food.
autorretrato-con-familia

The artist Guadalupe Carpio paints herself with her family, in a warm group portrait. She was one of the first Mexican women to study at the Academy of San Carlos in Mexico City. The picture shows her family around her. It's an unusual self-portrait.
giotto-and-cimabue

The young shepherd boy Giotto draws a sheep in the dirt as the great painter Cimabue watches in amazement. According to legend, Cimabue saw Giotto's talent and took him as a student. José María Obregón, a Mexican painter, painted this famous story in 1857. It's about discovering a gift.
the-wake

People gather in a dark house at night for a wake, in a quiet, sad scene. José María Jara, a Mexican painter, painted this in 1889. It shows the customs of mourning in Mexico. It's a moving picture of community.
el-valle-de-mexico

The great Valley of Mexico spreads out beneath a huge sky, with volcanoes, lakes and small villages. José María Velasco is the most famous Mexican landscape painter, and he painted this in 1877. He was also a scientist who studied plants and animals. It's a grand and loving portrait of his country.
gran-cometa-de-1882

A giant comet streaks across the night sky over the Mexican landscape. José María Velasco saw the Great Comet of 1882 and painted it. He was a scientist who knew a lot about astronomy. It's a beautiful picture of a real event.
the-dead-flower

A woman in a dress holds a wilted flower, with a sad, thoughtful look. Manuel Ocaranza was a Mexican painter who died young, at 31. The dead flower stands for lost love or the shortness of life. It's a famous romantic painting from Mexico.
